name: Introduction and overview — Baltimore-class Cruiser — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Baltimore-class Cruiser
description: Introduction and overview of the Baltimore-class Cruiser: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Baltimore class — 14 built — was the U.S. Navy's standard World War II heavy cruiser: 17,200 tons with nine 8-inch guns. Baltimores fought at Leyte Gulf, Iwo Jima, and Okinawa; several served in Korea. The class also parented the Oregon City and Des Moines designs. Baseline facts: U.S. WWII heavy cruiser; 14 built; nine 8-inch guns; Leyte Gulf and Okinawa..
